successors.name: Kingdom of Ireland
successors.text: Tyrone and its neighbours: 'fled in 1607 in what became known as the Flight of the Earls'; the earls' lands were then declared forfeit (Plantations page)

ledger.x: c. 465: Eógan mac Néill, the first ruler (infobox 'c. 465: Eógan mac Néill (first)'; 'Established: 5th century'). 'The kingdom represented the core homeland of the Cenél nEógain people of the Northern Uí Néill.' The page starts the territory in Inishowen and gives no year for Tyrone, so the land beyond Inishowen is…

By the 8th century: 'the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann' (Ulaid page); the Tir Eoghain page says 'The territory of Eoghan mac Neill was initially based in Inishowen and expanded out from there under his descendants' and gives no year.
735 to 827: 'From 735 they fell under the dominance of the Cenél nEógain, and by 827 had become their vassals.'
Page silent on the end of the vassalage: the Airgíalla kingdom 'was at its peak in the 12th century, under king Donnchad Ua Cerbaill' (reign 1130-1168/9), so 1130 is a bridge (confidence 1).
1593: Hugh O'Neill takes Tyrone and the Nine Years' War begins.

wars.name: Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: Hugh O'Neill's Ulster confederacy held out until 1603, when Tyrone submitted; the Treaty of Mellifont ended the war and 'by 1603 the entire country was under English rule'.

certainty.note: The page names counties, no frontier.
